          Women's Champions League: Five Subplots Ahead of Matchday 3
        
      
                          
                      Oct 27, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The UEFA Women's Champions League returns for Matchday 3 on Wednesday evening. What should you be keeping an eye on? We discuss the subplots ahead of this week's action.
The UEFA Women's Champions League returns this week and, with only six games in the league phase, Matchday 3 already represents the halfway point for Europe's elite.

Barcelona have made a flying start, winning both of their opening matches and scoring 11 goals in the process. They are the only side with maximum points, but behind them, the race for direct qualification to the quarter-finals is harder to call.
Chelsea and Arsenal have four points apiece, while Manchester City, Bayern München and OL Lyonnes are also unbeaten after two matches, albeit with City down in 10th after two draws.
According to the Opta supercomputer, Barcelona are overwhelming favourites to secure a top-four finish, while Arsenal and Manchester City already appear slightly up against it.
Let's dive into five key talking points ahead of MD3.

Alessia Russo is closing in on a place in the history books, with Arsenal’s clash against Benfica offering the England striker an opportunity to draw level with Fran Kirby as the highest-scoring English player in the history of the Champions League.
Russo has scored 20 goals in the UWCL, leaving her just one short of Kirby’s record of 21.

Although unbeaten so far, the Gunners have made an unconvincing start to the league phase. A late penalty secured a 1-0 victory over HB Køge on Matchday 1, before they surrendered a two-goal advantage to draw 2-2 with Paris FC.

Those performances have come amid an unusually subdued attacking start domestically. Arsenal have scored just seven goals in their opening seven WSL matches, with only five coming from open play. It's a modest return for a side who usually rank among the competition’s most prolific attacks, and Renée Slegers will be keen to build on the momentum of their North London Derby victory over Tottenham.

There are reasons for optimism here. Arsenal have won each of their last six home matches in the Champions League and scored in 15 consecutive group-stage or league-phase games in the competition. Benfica, meanwhile, have gone 10 European matches without keeping a clean sheet.
Russo also scored against the Portuguese side in Arsenal’s 2-0 victory in Lisbon last season, making them a familiar opponent as she approaches the landmark.

The Opta supercomputer gives Arsenal just a 28.7% chance of finishing in the top four and qualifying directly for the quarter-finals, projecting a final league-phase total of 10.4 points. With automatic qualification far from assured, securing maximum points against Benfica could prove crucial to their European ambitions.
Some might even argue that Arsenal’s most viable route to qualifying for next season’s Champions League could be to win the competition itself.
Chelsea’s pursuit of a first Champions League title continues, and it's underpinned by a remarkable level of consistency in the competition’s league/group phase.

The Blues have lost just one of their 32 group-stage matches in the competition, winning 23 and drawing eight. They are currently unbeaten in 26 consecutive games at this stage, a run stretching back to December 2021.
Their home record is even more formidable. Chelsea have never lost a group-stage or league-phase match on home soil, winning 12 and drawing four of their 16 fixtures.
They have carried that reliability into the current campaign, opening with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Austria Wien, before grinding out a goalless draw away to European heavyweights Lyon.

Despite dropping points in France, Chelsea remain well placed to progress directly to the quarter-finals. The Opta supercomputer gives them a 76.6% chance of finishing in the top four, projecting a final league-phase total of 13.13 points.
Chelsea’s wait for their first European crown goes on, but their consistency at this stage of the competition continues to provide a strong platform for another serious challenge.
